title: Graph Engineering approval grant
description: The exact document a human authority produces to decide one approval request, and the frozen `data` payload of the HumanInputReceived event. A grant echoes every binding field of its request and carries the request's identity and document hash, so a grant issued for one request cannot satisfy another. Five decisions exist and only 'approve' and 'supersede' confer authority. See approval-semantics.md.

apiVersion.description: Ownership discriminator. A document is a claimed approval grant if and only if it carries this exact value.

grantId.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 over the domain-separated framing of every other member of this document. Because the identity covers the whole body, two grants with equal grantId have equal canonical bytes up to a SHA-256 collision, which is what makes the duplicate-presentation rule a byte-exact replay test rather than a name match.

requestId.description: Identity of the request this grant decides. Recomputed from the outstanding request and compared; never trusted as carried.

requestHash.description: Domain-separated canonical hash of the complete request document, including its own requestId. requestId binds the request's inputs; requestHash binds its exact bytes. Both are checked, because a document can differ in a member that the identity framing does not cover.

subject.description: Verbatim echo of the request's subject. Any difference is a binding mismatch, not a narrowing.

decision.description: Closed five-member decision vocabulary. 'approve' and 'supersede' confer authority; 'reject', 'revoke' and 'expire' are refusals and MUST carry the empty scope. There is no default and no sixth member, so no absence of information can become a grant.

approverPrincipal.description: The deciding principal. The 'system:' namespace is structurally excluded here as it is in the authority allowlist, so no runtime-synthesized identity can decide.

grantedScope.description: The authority actually conferred. It MUST be a subset of the request's requestedScope under the member-wise rule in approval-semantics.md, and for a superseding grant also a subset of the grant it supersedes.

supersedesGrantId.description: Required if and only if decision is 'revoke' or 'supersede'; forbidden otherwise. It names the grant currently in effect for this request.

confirmation.description: Required if and only if the decision confers authority and the request's sideEffects are not 'none'; forbidden otherwise. It records what the approver actually verified about the external system, and it is the only thing that may authorize re-firing a non-idempotent effect.

Explicit confirmation for a resumed node whose committed sideEffects are not 'none'. 'new-attempt' re-fires the effect and is admissible only against a verified not-applied observation; 'adopt-applied' continues past an effect the approver verified as applied and never fabricates the lost output.

sideEffects.description: Verbatim echo of the request's sideEffects. 'none' is absent here because a 'none' request forbids the confirmation block entirely.

observedExternalState.description: What the approver verified about the external system. 'unverified' can never authorize anything; it exists so an approver can say so truthfully instead of guessing.

humanInputReceivedData.description: Frozen `data` payload of the HumanInputReceived event. Exactly one grant per event; a runtime never batches decisions into one event, because the ledger folds one committed grant per appended event and a batch would make the duplicate rule ambiguous. spec/event.schema.json still declares an open `data` object; the integration lane owns referencing this definition from it, and this contract does not modify that file.
